sources.title: Detect and Avoid System
sources.jurisdiction: Vendor account; US and international UAS context
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected full public page, including historical DAA/ATAR description, claimed 2025 TSO target, sensor architecture and ACAS Xu discussion.

regions.locator: Lines 7-14, DAA standardization and proposed certification
regions.excerpt: TSO-C211 for DAA, and TSO-C212 for ATAR systems
The DAA system must detect and avoid cooperative ... and non-cooperative ... aircraft

sources.limitations: Vendor marketing and product description. It does not establish that a TSO authorization was actually issued, that the system is installed on a civil aircraft, or that operations are unrestricted. The page contains historical/forward-looking statements.

sources.title: FAA/GA-ASI DAA Sensor Model Validation Final Report ASI-23126 Rev A
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected pages 5-7 of the 22-page PDF: purpose, flight test, TSO-C211 context, sensor types and model-validation scope.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, executive summary and introduction
regions.excerpt: The team collected sensor data (ATAR, ADS-B, and Active Surveillance)

regions.locator: PDF p. 6, civil-approval and operational-scope discussion
regions.excerpt: its application in the National Airspace System (NAS) is still in its infancy

sources.limitations: A 2022 research deliverable and not a current product approval, installation approval, aircraft type certificate or operational authorization. The report references associated reports not inspected here.

sources.title: Technical Standard Orders (TSO)

regions.excerpt: Receiving a TSO Authorization is not an approval to install and use the article in the aircraft

sources.limitations: General explanatory page, not a specific article authorization or aircraft installation record.

sources.inspection_scope: Inspected Appendix C listing of TSO titles.

regions.locator: PDF p. 47, Appendix C TSO table

sources.title: Draft TSO-C211a, Detect and Avoid (DAA) Systems
sources.jurisdiction: US civil aviation; draft certification standard
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected FAA search extract for applicability, draft effective-date placeholder, DO-365C Change 1 dependency, and functional classes including ACAS Xu.

regions.excerpt: This TSO is for manufacturers applying for a TSO authorization (TSOA) or letter of design approval (LODA)

sources.limitations: The retrieved document visibly contains an mm/dd/25 effective-date placeholder and bracketed transition date. Treat as draft/proposed material, not as evidence that the revision is effective or that any article is approved.

sources.title: Draft TSO-C212a, Air-to-Air Radar (ATAR) for Traffic Surveillance
sources.jurisdiction: US civil aviation; draft certification standard
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected PDF pp. 1-8: draft status, radar classes, cooperative/non-cooperative detection, failure classifications, DO-178C/DO-254 data and separate installation approval.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 1-3, radar functions and failure classifications
regions.excerpt: The on-board radar complements other on-board airborne surveillance sensors by providing detection of non-cooperative traffic
Installation of this article requires separate approval.

sources.limitations: Draft document with placeholder effective date. Its requirements are not evidence of authorization, installation or operational approval. RTCA documents referenced by the draft were not redistributed or inspected.

sources.title: FAA Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected executive summary and PDF pp. 8-11, 24-30 covering learned versus learning AI, incremental assurance, RTA, formal/numerical methods, black-box validation and planned policy work.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 10-11, learned versus learning AI
regions.excerpt: each new version is subjected to safety assurance
Software Runtime Assurance in AI
Policy statement to inform applicants that plan to use AI in their systems ... discuss a certification path with the FAA early

sources.limitations: A roadmap and research/policy plan, not a certification standard or authorization. Dates and planned outputs are subject to change; detailed technical methods remain under development.

sources.title: EASA Artificial Intelligence Concept Paper Issue 2
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected EASA landing page summary and publication metadata; linked PDF retrieval was rate-limited and its full text was not inspected.

regions.excerpt: deepens the exploration of 'learning assurance', 'AI explainability' and 'ethics-based assessment'

sources.limitations: Landing-page summary only. Do not attribute detailed requirements, approval status or Level 2 boundaries beyond the summary until the PDF is captured and reviewed.

sources.title: EASA Artificial Intelligence Concept Paper Proposed Issue 3
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected EASA landing page title, date and download listing; PDF and comment-response spreadsheet were not retrieved due HTTP 429.

regions.excerpt: EASA Artificial Intelligence Concept Paper — Proposed Issue 3

sources.limitations: Proposed document status and existence only. It is not a final guidance publication and no technical proposition from the PDF is supported here.

sources.title: Detect and Avoid Policy Concept Consultation Response Summary CAP3127
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected full 26-page PDF, especially pp. 3-5, 12-16 and next-steps discussion, covering equipment reliance, metrics, encounter sets and policy test phase.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 12-13, equipment reliance and assurance
regions.excerpt: The DAA policy and assurance process is founded on established principles from the Airborne Collision Avoidance System (ACAS)
NMAC is used instead as a proxy for MAC
status of the DAA Policy Concept and next steps

sources.limitations: Consultation response and policy-development document, not a final operational approval. It records stakeholder feedback and initial CAA responses; planned policy remains subject to later publication and testing.

sources.title: FAA authorizes Zipline commercial BVLOS delivery
sources.jurisdiction: US civil UAS; Salt Lake City operations
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected FAA announcement and its linked approval-letter targets; regulations.gov pages returned 403. The announcement states scope and directs readers to the letters.

regions.excerpt: without visual observers

sources.limitations: Announcement establishes FAA public description of a scoped authorization. Linked letters and conditions must be obtained before asserting exact DAA architecture, aircraft configuration, current validity or all-airspace operation.

sources.title: FAA BEYOND program status page

sources.title: Protector programme and certification statements
sources.inspection_scope: Inspected government announcement describing trials, remote piloting and intended NATO safety/certification status; no certificate instrument inspected.

regions.excerpt: Protector will be certified to stringent NATO safety and certification standards allowing it to operate in the UK and European civilian airspace

sources.limitations: Government programme statement, not the Military Type Certificate or civil operational authorization. The wording is prospective as of 2023 and should not be used to claim a current unrestricted civil approval.
